note: Documents we know exist, or expect to exist, and are waiting on. Each one is a short lookup rather than a piece of research. check-staleness warns once checkAfter has passed, so nothing here can quietly rot in a markdown file. Adding a row is cheap; leaving a known gap unrecorded is not.

items.what: The Welsh National Minimum Allowance letter for 2025/26. ACCEPTED GAP as at 3 September 2026 after three unsuccessful searches. Two routes remain, neither requiring more searching. First, a guessable path: the 2024/25 letter also exists at /sites/default/files/2024-05/NMA%20Letter%202024-25%20-%20English%20(E)_0.pdf on The Fostering Network, so try /sites/default/files/2025-04/, 2025-05/ and 2025-06/ with the year changed. Second, and more likely to work: ask. The letters go out by email, which is why they are not on the open web. The addresses are printed on the 2024/25 letter itself: plantsynderbyngofal@llyw.cymru, and Alistair Davey, Deputy Director Enabling People, Alistair.Davey@gov.wales. One email would likely close both this and the 2026/27 letter.
items.why: Searched to exhaustion: The Fostering Network media library, the govdelivery UKWALES_CSSIW_INT account, Care Inspectorate Wales archives in both languages, gov.wales and llyw.cymru written statements and decision reports, Foster Wales and twelve local authorities, council committee repositories, and National Archives snapshots from February and March 2025. The govdelivery bulletin IDs are non-sequential hex and cannot be derived. A 2.6 per cent uplift was announced in February 2025 and figures of 224 / 204 / 255 are reported, inversion intact, but only from a reproduced table and not from the Welsh Government letter. Secondary, so not usable. The cost of the gap is one year of Welsh backdating, which the site already handles by naming the excluded year. That is a far smaller problem than publishing a rate we cannot source.

items.what: The outcome of the Welsh consultation on the Part 6 and Special Guardianship Orders codes of practice.
items.why: The consultation closed on 7 April 2026. The draft would require all services to pay the national minimum allowance. Until the outcome is published nothing on this site may state it as the law, and when it lands the Wales pages need rewriting.

items.what: The final version of Leeds City Council's revised special guardianship support offer.
items.why: Leeds says its financial support information is under review, so the March 2024 offer is served with an on-screen note saying so. The Child Benefit position is deliberately not stated, because the only source for it is a freedom of information response that itself says the policy is under review.

items.what: The final Special Guardianship Orders Code of Practice for Wales.
items.why: The consultation that closed on 7 April 2026 covers TWO codes, and one of them is the SGO code. That is the Welsh equivalent of the statutory guidance the whole English side of this site rests on, so when it is finalised the Wales pages need more than a rates refresh. Tracked separately from the Part 6 code for that reason. As at 2 September 2026 the responses are still being reviewed, and a fuller review was signalled for early in the next Senedd term.

items.what: Lincolnshire County Council's published Special Guardianship Allowance Assessment Framework, which describes the DfE means test model as non-statutory guidance in its own words. Find a permanent address for it.
items.why: CoramBAAF Practice Note 75 is the only source cited for the proposition that the means test model is not law. It resolves publicly but sits on a members-area path and could be withdrawn without notice. A council conceding the point in its own published policy is a better citation than a practice note, and it removes a single point of failure.
